co_eagle_rock.blurb: Eagle Rock is a steep buttress in the lower part of Boulder Canyon, a short drive from town. Most of the climbing is bolted, with a smaller number of trad lines and a few boulder problems, and the difficulty skews hard: a big share of the routes fall in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, so it suits strong sport climbers. Eagle Eyes, Golden Eagle and Buddha Belly are among the draws, and Dharma Punks and Egalitarian offer longer, multi-pitch outings. Dharma Punks borrows the bolted first pitch of Eagle Hardware, then keeps going up the middle of the buttress, so expect an adventurous day with rappel stations rather than a quick lap.

co_child_free_zone_aka_parkway_crags.blurb: Child Free Zone is a two-tiered band of cliff on the far eastern edge of North Table Mountain, just outside Golden. Sport and trad share the wall, and the lines are generally short and stiff, with plenty in the 5.10 range and a handful of 5.11s and 5.12s. Mohare Eclaire and Monkey Puzzle are the hard sport draws, while Scream Amy is a trad option at the easier end of the 5.10s. The wall catches sun and warms up early, which makes it a better pick for cool months than for midsummer afternoons.
co_child_free_zone_aka_parkway_crags.approach: Follow the trail from the lot to the cliff, then turn right at the foot of the wall and keep walking along its base, past an arete and a gully, until the path ends at the right side of the crag.

co_canal_zone_the.blurb: The Canal Zone is the first crag on the left as you head up Clear Creek Canyon, and it is one of the canyon's friendliest places to start leading bolts. Nearly all of it is single-pitch sport with a few trad lines mixed in, and the grades center on 5.8 through 5.10, with a handful of 5.11s such as Walking With A Ghost and Snake Eyes. Made In The Shade is a popular easier pick. The wall stays shaded for most of the day, which helps in summer heat but can feel chilly in colder months. Rattlesnakes are known to use the approach in warm weather.
co_canal_zone_the.parking_note: Use the Tunnel 1 trailhead pullout just inside the canyon mouth on US-6; it is a one-way loop with a toilet.
co_canal_zone_the.approach: Cross the footbridge from the pullout, take the stone steps on the right, pass through the gate on the left and follow the path roughly a third of a mile to the right end of the crag.

co_west_side.blurb: The West Side is a granite cliff on the far bank of the canyon at Lemon Reservoir, above Durango. It mixes bolted lines with crack climbs, so a light rack is worth bringing for some routes. Most of the climbing sits in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Chucky Bill, Cape of Good Hope and Vertical Alluvium are trad picks, while Bonsai, Lemon Peel and Via Manolo are sport. The cliff gets morning sun and afternoon shade, and the high, cool setting makes it a summer escape from lower-elevation heat. Reaching the base takes a bit of effort, including a short descent on a fixed rope.
co_west_side.parking_note: Park in the Burnt Timber Trailhead lot, just before the entrance to Transfer Park Campground at the end of the forest road along the reservoir.

co_eureka.blurb: Eureka is a high-elevation ice area in the San Juan Mountains, above Silverton at roughly 9,800 feet near the old mining townsite. Climbs of all sizes line the Animas River drainage, from a short pitch minutes from the car to waterfalls that approach a thousand feet. Most of what is here is water ice around WI3 and WI4, with a few steeper pitches and a small group of mixed lines. The climbs form in winter, and avalanches often run down the same paths as the ice, so snow stability and timing matter as much as the climbing itself.
co_eureka.approach: Drive up the main drainage on the plowed road as far as you can, then walk the rest of the road. The ice is visible from the road, and the nearest pitch is a few minutes from the lot.

co_death_valley.blurb: Death Valley is a sunny sport crag on the south side of Clear Creek Canyon near Tunnel 5, at the upstream end of the same cliff as the Graveyard. Routes are one pitch and roughly 40 to 100 feet tall, almost all bolted, with grades running from easy to the 5.12s and the biggest group in the 5.10 range. Brazen Bull, a 5.9+, is the standout moderate. Because the wall takes the afternoon sun, it is best known as a winter and shoulder-season option rather than a midsummer one.

co_pear_the.blurb: The Pear is a clean granite buttress on Lumpy Ridge, just west of the Book. It is almost entirely trad, with slabs, dihedrals and some overhangs, and routes usually run two to three pitches, with summit lines stretching longer. Most of the climbing is between 5.6 and 5.10, with a few harder pitches mixed in, which makes it a good place for moderate multi-pitch. Heavenly Journey and Whole Thing are the named classics. Many routes can be walked off after two pitches, but the descent is involved, so study it before leaving the ground.

co_arrowhead.blurb: Arrowhead is a granite spire above Black Lake in upper Glacier Gorge, Rocky Mountain National Park. The rock is blocky and grippy, and most routes are alpine-style trad of four or five pitches, with a cluster in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. Glacier Gorge Traverse is the easy classic at 5.7, while Arrowplane, Ithaca, The Godfather and Airhead take on harder terrain. In winter and spring, The Hourglass Couloir and Deborah offer snow, ice and mixed climbing. It is a long way in, so expect an early start, and afternoon storms are common in summer.
co_arrowhead.approach: From the Glacier Gorge trailhead, hike past Mills Lake to Black Lake, skirt the lake's east side, and follow grass ramps up to the base of the formation.

co_mine_hole_crag.blurb: Mine Hole Crag is a small, single-pitch crag about eight and a half miles up Boulder Canyon, beside an old abandoned mine on the north side of the highway. It leans toward trad, with some sport lines, and routes are 30 to 100 feet tall. The grades span the 5.6 to 5.12 range, though most fall between 5.8 and 5.10. The face stays in morning shade, which helps on warm days. Rock at the tops of some routes is loose, and rockfall is a real hazard, so helmets and care around the ledges are a good idea.
co_mine_hole_crag.parking_note: Use the roadside pullout on the left past the Narrows, shared with the trails to the Boulderado and Animal World cliffs.
co_mine_hole_crag.approach: Take the path up the hill on the left side of the Boulderado, skirt the base of the rock band, and scramble up a loose gully to the mine entrance, with the crag about 100 feet west of it.

co_highlands_aka_highlander_the.blurb: The Highlands, or Highlander, is a hard sport crag on a hill above the New River Wall in Clear Creek Canyon. The wall runs from vertical to overhanging, often with small roofs, and the bolting is generous. Grades start around 5.10 and climb into the 5.13s, with most routes in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. Peer Review, Not One Of Us and Peer Pressure are well-regarded 5.12s, while Peer 42, The White Whale and Peer Bastard offer 5.13 projects. The right side of the cliff is very solid and the left side is looser. It gets plenty of sun, so it is a classic winter crag.
co_highlands_aka_highlander_the.parking_note: Park in the large paved pullout just before Tunnel 2.
co_highlands_aka_highlander_the.approach: Walk up the road on the right, cross the bridge, then follow the climbers' trail downstream past Twitch Rock to a flat spot and take the left fork uphill for roughly 400 yards of slabby path to the cliff.
